dish: Wok-hei charred char kway teow (from S$4)
n: Ang Mo Kio Fried Kway Teow
address: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-22, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
w: An elderly couple has fried this heritage char kway teow for 40-odd years, opening just 3.5 hours a day — the longest queue in 724 AMK Central, with senior regulars waiting 30 minutes at lunch for smoky, lard-slicked plates.

dish: Mee rebus with a nearly 60-year-old gravy recipe
address: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-01, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
w: Started by the late Haji Yunos Ahmad as a 1965 pushcart at Hastings Road and now run by the third generation, this stall pours a thick, spiced sweet-potato mee rebus gravy that ranks among Singapore's most storied — also known for its satay and soto.

dish: Hand-scraped pure yellowtail fishball mee pok
address: Blk 158 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, #01-590 (coffeeshop beside Mayflower Market), S560158
w: Two brothers from Kuantan scrape yellowtail by hand daily — fishballs of pure fish, salt and pepper with no flour or filler, tossed Malaysian-style with black sauce and shallot oil. Sells out within four hours; closed Mondays.

dish: Char siew, crispy sio bak & roast duck rice
address: Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, #01-84, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628
w: AMK's most popular roast-meat stall for two decades, drawing long queues for glossy char siew, shatter-crisp sio bak and a paper-skinned roast duck that fans rate above town shops — the classic combo plate is S$4.50.

dish: Claypot crab bee hoon soup (milky crab broth)
address: Blk 232 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-1222, S560232
w: A crab specialist since 1979 (Michelin Plate 2019) whose signature claypot crab bee hoon simmers over 20 crab shells into a rich, sweet milky broth soaked into glass noodles — plus chilli, black pepper and salted-egg crabs. Come early; the queue forms fast.

dish: Coin prata set & 19 kinds of prata
address: Jin Fa Kopitiam, Blk 24 Sin Ming Road, #01-51, S570024
w: On the Sin Ming edge of AMK, this corner stall traces back to a 1933 street-prata grandfather; the third generation flips 19 kinds and a famed hand-rolled Coin Prata set (S$4 for 6) that queues form for at breakfast.

dish: Small crispy 'Jalan Kayu' roti prata since 1960
address: 237 Jalan Kayu, S799462
w: The stall that made 'Jalan Kayu prata' a Singapore byword — serving small, round, crispy prata (plus murtabak, mee goreng and biryani) since the 1960s, so copied that it signboards itself the 'Original Prata Shop'. Open 24 hours.

dish: 'Power' mee rebus with satay peanut gravy & spiced chicken
address: Chong Boon Market & Food Centre, #01-01, Blk 453A Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560453
w: Around since 1957 and now third-generation, Rahim's Straits Times-featured 'Power' mee rebus layers savoury satay peanut sauce and spiced chicken over the usual gravy — long queues at this Chong Boon stall for mee rebus and mee soto.

dish: Dry-style fried Hokkien prawn mee with robust prawn stock
address: Mayflower Market & Food Centre, #01-39, Blk 162 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560162
w: Hawker Ah Ho learned the wok some 30 years ago at a famed Bukit Batok stall and now fries a leaning-wet Hokkien mee of yellow noodles and thin bee hoon in umami prawn stock — once named a top-10 Hokkien mee by Lianhe Wanbao.

dish: Springy fishball mee pok in lightly sweet pork broth
n: Song Heng Fishball Minced Meat Noodle
address: Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, #01-75, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628
w: The longest queue at 628 with almost no publicity — a balanced chilli-vinegar dry mee pok with bouncy fishballs and a lightly sweet pork soup; fishballs regularly sell out by 11am. Closed Tuesdays.

dish: Signature seafood noodle (bak-chor-mee style with seafood)
address: Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628
w: Millennial hawker Max left a finance job in 2020 and, after training at Hock Heng, opened this long-queue stall; the Signature Seafood Noodle (from S$5) plays like bak chor mee but with seafood in place of pork.

dish: Wok-hei fried Hokkien mee (single-item menu)
address: Food Loft Kopitiam, Ang Mo Kio Ave 8, Singapore
w: Two Gen-Z hawkers both named Jie fry one dish only — a wok-hei Hokkien mee on a wide stove that chars the noodles before the homemade prawn stock goes in, with fresh pork lard and house chilli. Hour-long queues since 2024.

dish: Salted-egg prawns & pumpkin prawns
address: Blk 202 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-1690, S560202
w: A family zi char in a HDB coffeeshop since 2003, beloved for crunchy salted-egg prawns, pumpkin prawns, Dong Po pork belly and the usual chilli/salted-egg crabs — a reliable AMK feast spot.

dish: Teochew-style chilli crab & classic zi char
address: Ang Mo Kio, Singapore (coffeeshop zi char; block to verify)
w: An old-school Teochew zi char in AMK serving chilli crab and Teochew classics at neighbourhood prices — a longstanding local favourite for casual family dinners.

dish: Fried chicken & waffles, big breakfast (free-flow ice cream)
address: Blk 202 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-1682, S560202
w: A retro void-deck cafe doing nett-price Western brunch — fried chicken and waffles (S$13.90), eggs benedict, fish and chips — with free-flow ice cream thrown in with every main.

dish: Peppery bak kut teh & braised pig trotter
address: Teck Ghee Court Market & Food Centre, #01-04, Blk 341 Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, S560341
w: A lunchtime-queue fixture at Teck Ghee for peppery Singapore-style bak kut teh (S$8) and a fork-tender braised pig's trotter (S$7) in a dark, wine-scented lor bak gravy.

dish: Teochew porridge with 30-plus fresh-cooked sides
address: Cheng San Market & Cooked Food Centre, Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, Singapore
w: Twenty years of Teochew-style porridge and a spread of 30-plus sides — fresh fish, fried meatballs, braised pork belly — one of Cheng San's most reliable old-school stalls.

dish: XL hand-made halal fishball noodles
address: Cheng San Centre, Blk 532 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, #01-2495, S560532
w: One of few halal-certified fishball noodle stalls, a hotspot for the Malay community — large hand-scooped fishballs on a family recipe, around S$5.50-6.50. Moved to Cheng San/AMK from Upper Thomson in Dec 2022.

dish: Satay bee hoon in thick peanut-satay gravy
address: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-12, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
w: Thin rice vermicelli drowned in a thick, peanut-heavy satay sauce with cuttlefish, prawns, pork, tau pok and kang kong (from ~S$4) — rated by some as the best satay bee hoon around.

dish: Herbal braised duck with rice (10-plus herbs)
address: Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, #01-20, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, S560226
w: Over four decades of herbal braised duck at Kebun Baru — the braise draws on more than ten herbs for a deep, aromatic gravy over rice or noodles.

dish: Dry mee pok with house chilli-vinegar-tomato sauce
address: Sembawang Hills Food Centre, #01-04, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419
w: Sembawang Hills' standout fishball noodle — a dry mee pok tossed in a house blend of chilli, vinegar and tomato, with fishballs, fishcake and pork liver served in a light porky soup.

dish: Traditional Hainanese chicken rice
address: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
w: A traditional Hainanese chicken rice counter that regularly makes the round-ups of 724 AMK Central's best — poached chicken and fragrant rice at heartland prices.

dish: Fried Hokkien prawn mee, carrot cake & oyster omelette
address: Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628
w: A 628 stall specialising in the trio of fried Hokkien prawn mee, fried carrot cake and oyster omelette — a solid all-rounder in one of AMK's most food-dense hawker centres.

dish: Lor mee & laksa
n: Ang Mo Kio Loh Mee Laksa
address: Chong Boon Market & Food Centre, #01-17, Blk 453A Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560453
w: An elderly couple has run this Chong Boon stall for more than a decade, doing two things well — a thick-gravy lor mee and a coconutty laksa.

dish: Red grouper fish-head soup
address: Chong Boon Market & Food Centre, #01-10, Blk 453A Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560453
w: Known at Chong Boon for an affordable, generous red grouper fish-head soup (around S$10) — a comforting, clean-tasting bowl.

dish: Silky poached-chicken rice (morning)
address: Chong Boon Market & Food Centre, #01-19, Blk 453A Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560453
w: A morning go-to at Chong Boon for silky, smooth poached chicken and fragrant rice.

dish: Dry tossed noodles (long queue)
address: Chong Boon Market & Food Centre, #01-39, Blk 453A Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560453
w: A 12-year Chong Boon stall that draws one of the centre's longest queues for its dry-tossed noodles.

dish: Wanton noodle (31-year stall)
address: Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, #01-05, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, S560226
w: A 31-year Kebun Baru stall serving a tidy small wanton noodle from S$3.50 — old-school springy mee and char siew.

dish: Handmade fishball & meatball noodle
n: Foo Hing Handmade Fishball & Meatball Noodle
address: Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, #01-01, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, S560226
w: A Kebun Baru fixture for handmade fishballs and meatballs in a clean noodle bowl — one of the centre's most-recommended stalls.

dish: $1.30-a-basket dim sum, open 24 hours
address: Blk 555 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, #01-1936, S560555
w: A no-frills 24-hour spot where every basket of dim sum is S$1.30 (buy 10, get 1 free) — fried prawn dumplings and siew mai the picks; not fine dining, but unbeatable value.

dish: Fresh sliced-fish seafood soup
address: Sembawang Hills Food Centre, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419
w: A perennial peak-hour queue at Sembawang Hills for a fresh sliced-fish seafood soup — ladle it over ke kou mian or bee hoon to soak up the broth.
